stages.title: Robust inference and model comparison: research guide
stages.html:
Robust inference and model comparison

Match covariance estimators and comparison tools to the maintained model.

Model-based information, sandwich uncertainty, likelihood-ratio tests, and information criteria answer different questions.

Workflow. Use sandwich uncertainty under misspecification while stating the pseudo-true target.

Diagnostic: Inspect score covariance versus Hessian curvature. The main failure to avoid is model-based precision that assumes a false conditional variance.

stages.title: Robust inference and model comparison: worked Python model
stages.note: Run the reproducible example, then change one assumption and compare the output.
stages.code:
import numpy as np
y = np.array([1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1])
grid = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 181)
loglike = np.array([(y*np.log(p) + (1-y)*np.log(1-p)).sum() for p in grid])
p_hat = grid[np.argmax(loglike)]
print(f"Grid MLE: {p_hat:.3f}")
print(f"Sample mean: {y.mean():.3f}")

stages.title: Likelihood model comparison: model decision
stages.note: A team is about to report results without checking nesting, parameter counts, and out-of-sample loss.

steps.prompt: What is the best next action?
choices: Match LR tests to nesting and use information criteria for predictive tradeoffs.
Increase decimal precision and report immediately.
Drop observations until the preferred coefficient appears.

steps.prompt: Which risk should the final report address explicitly?
choices: Only whether the sample mean is positive.
comparing non-nested models with an invalid reference distribution
Whether every coefficient has the same sign.
